authorship.author: OpenAI Codex
authorship.record_epistemics: Invented story-world statuses, not real verification claims.
authorship.label_basis: Authored from explicit record text and declared scope rules before retrieval output.
authorship.split_policy: Distinct authored family/story sets allocated before tuning; no family crosses splits.
authorship.blinding_limit: The fixture author can see both splits. Family separation is not an independently curated blind benchmark.
authorship.coverage_limit: Synthetic English technical stories; not representative production evidence or authenticated authorization.
authorship.relevance_convention: 3: direct answer or independently requested component; 2: explicit partial answer or corroboration; 1: useful illustration/context; absent: nonrelevant or ineligible. Labels include explicit corroboration but remain fallible synthetic judgments.
authorship.workspace_pool_policy: Ordinary queries allow five related projects and their authors, with tasks unrestricted. Explicit scope/history questions may have small eligible sets; report them separately.
authorship.levels: 1: synthetic episode/fact; 2: private preference or synthesis; 3: verified story-world shared decision owned by Hive. These labels do not execute actual storage or promotion.
authorship.provenance_representation: Source IDs and availability are symbolic story-world provenance, not real retained source files or human verification. No external source content is asserted.

records.title: Export edge limit
records.body: Canvas clamps either raster export edge to 8192 pixels. The limit applies after scaling; a wide but short image can still exceed it. The encoder returns EXPORT_EDGE_LIMIT before allocating the destination buffer.

records.title: Where export dimensions are checked
records.body: The function checkRasterBounds in src/export/raster_bounds.ts checks the scaled width and height. It runs before encodePng and emits EXPORT_EDGE_LIMIT with the offending edge.

records.title: Previous export ceiling
records.body: The first Canvas exporter allowed an edge of 4096 pixels. Large poster requests were rejected even when they fit the newer memory budget.

records.title: Poster export capacity decision
records.body: The team selected the 8192-pixel ceiling after budgeting a single RGBA destination surface. The change replaces the earlier 4096-pixel restriction; it does not promise unlimited poster dimensions.

records.title: Iris prefers visible export sizing
records.body: For the image-export task, Iris wants the final pixel dimensions shown beside the scale control. A silent downscale is unacceptable because print layouts depend on the requested dimensions.

records.title: Preview edge policy
records.body: Canvas preview thumbnails stop at 1024 pixels on the long edge. This restriction belongs to the preview task and does not define downloadable export size.

records.title: Canvas export service at the museum
records.body: The museum's unrelated Canvas kiosk exports postcards with a 2048-pixel edge. Its TIFF writer uses a separate color profile.

records.title: Portrait export measurement
records.body: A synthetic portrait at 3000 by 7000 pixels passed the bounds check at scale one; scale two was rejected. This observation confirms scale is applied before checking each edge.

records.title: Possible transparent pixel optimization
records.body: Iris suspects fully transparent margins could be trimmed to permit larger apparent canvases. No implementation or memory measurements support that idea.

records.title: Card refund interval
records.body: Ledger permits a card refund during the first thirty calendar days after capture. Authorization time is not the start of this interval.

records.title: Refund age calculation
records.body: refundAgeDays in payments/refunds/age.py compares capture_date with the merchant's local business date. REFUND_TOO_OLD is raised after day thirty.

records.title: Partial refund accounting
records.body: Each partial refund subtracts from the captured balance. Multiple partial refunds are allowed while their total does not exceed the original capture.

records.title: Chargeback handling
records.body: A chargeback freezes self-service refunds until the dispute task releases the payment. The operator can read the payment but cannot issue another partial refund.

records.title: Former seven-day card rule
records.body: The initial pilot allowed card refunds for only seven days from capture.

records.title: Thirty-day rollout
records.body: The thirty-day card policy replaced the seven-day pilot after the merchant agreement changed. Store-credit returns were not part of this rollout.

records.title: Store-credit expiry
records.body: The store-credit task issues return vouchers that expire after ninety days. A voucher is not a reversal of the card capture.

records.title: Ledger library returns
records.body: The Library project calls its circulation log Ledger. Books may be returned after fourteen days without a late fee.

records.title: Partial refund replay
records.body: A synthetic capture of forty units accepted refunds of ten and twenty. An additional fifteen-unit refund was refused because only ten remained.

records.title: Holiday extension idea
records.body: Tomas suggested excluding public holidays when counting refund age. The proposal has no accepted policy or calendar implementation.

records.title: Webhook retry schedule
records.body: Harbor retries temporary webhook failures after two, ten, and forty minutes. A successful acknowledgment ends the schedule; the receiver must answer with a 2xx status.

records.title: Delivery attempt ledger
records.body: appendDeliveryAttempt in delivery/attempt_log.ts writes the destination, attempt number, and response class. It does not store the receiver's response body.

records.title: Permanent delivery failures
records.body: HTTP 410 closes a webhook subscription immediately. Other 4xx responses enter the rejected queue for operator review; they do not follow the temporary retry schedule.

records.title: Callback relay diagnostic journal
records.body:
The Harbor relay receives events from several business tasks and serializes each delivery into a small envelope. A run begins by recording a destination and an opaque event key; payload construction happens before the transport loop. The operator view groups attempts by subscription rather than by the producer's internal task name.

During the first synthetic drill, a receiver alternated between successful acknowledgments and temporary server failures. The attempt ledger preserved the response class, and the dashboard showed the delay until the next scheduled attempt. These observations helped explain queue occupancy but did not establish a policy for permanently rejected destinations. A second drill removed a subscription after all its pending events were drained.

Several earlier notes focused on dashboard timestamps, log colors, and the order in which rows appeared. None of those details determines whether a resumed delivery repeats an already accepted event. The response body was deliberately omitted from the ledger, so diagnosis used the status class and stable envelope key instead. The journal also records that destination edits create a new subscription version.

The decisive recovery rule is at the end of the drill: after an acknowledgment has been durably recorded, restarting the relay must not resend that event. The recovery cursor advances from the acknowledged attempt, not from the last event fetched from the producer.

records.title: Pilot retry spacing
records.body: Harbor's pilot repeated temporary failures every minute for three attempts.

records.title: Backoff change rationale
records.body: The two-ten-forty-minute schedule replaced the one-minute pilot to reduce pressure on recovering receivers.

records.title: Harbor import retry policy
records.body: The import task retries a failed CSV parse only after the operator changes the input. It never waits on a timer.

records.title: Sana's delivery log preference
records.body: Sana wants destination and response class visible in the delivery log. She does not want response bodies copied into the operator panel.

records.title: Receiver body retention claim
records.body: A draft runbook claims full receiver responses are retained for seven days, but its example attachment was lost and the draft has no approval.

records.title: Withdrawn retry-everything advice
records.body: An old support note told operators to retry every response, including HTTP 410. That advice was withdrawn because it reactivated removed subscriptions.

records.title: Route catalog root
records.body: Atlas resolves route documents beneath catalog/routes. User-facing route names are not filesystem paths and may contain spaces.

records.title: Canonical route path helper
records.body: canonicalRoutePath in routing/path_policy.rs converts a route slug into a file beneath catalog/routes. A resolved path outside that root returns RoutePathOutsideCatalog.

records.title: Display-name aliases
records.body: The route display name North Pass has aliases Northern Crossing and Ridge Link. All three refer to the same hiking route in Atlas's summer catalog.

records.title: North Pass winter route
records.body: The winter-planning task uses North Pass for a snowshoe route that stops at the lower hut. It is not the summer hiking traverse.

records.title: North Pass transit stop
records.body: Metro's North Pass stop is an underground platform on the copper line. It has no hiking route file.

records.title: Flat route storage
records.body: The first catalog placed route files directly in catalog, alongside image thumbnails.

records.title: Route directory migration
records.body: Moving route documents into catalog/routes separated them from thumbnails. Existing display-name aliases remained valid after the migration.

records.title: Alias lookup observation
records.body: In the synthetic summer catalog, searching Ridge Link returned the North Pass hiking route and its route document.

records.title: Nico's route labeling preference
records.body: Nico prefers the canonical route name first, followed by known aliases in parentheses. File slugs should stay out of the public title.

records.title: Lea's release-note style
records.body: Lea prefers release notes to lead with the user-visible result and then one concrete example. Internal ticket numbers belong in a final references line.

records.title: Release note length decision
records.body: Routine fixes get one paragraph in Quill release notes. Breaking changes may use a migration checklist because a paragraph can hide required user actions.

records.title: Release note formatter
records.body: renderReleaseEntry in notes/render_entry.py keeps the result sentence before the example and renders references last. It accepts a migration_steps list only for breaking changes.

records.title: Former ticket-first style
records.body: The earlier release-note template began each entry with the internal ticket number.

records.title: Readability revision
records.body: Lea replaced ticket-first headings with result-first entries after external readers could not interpret ticket codes.

records.title: Incident report writing style
records.body: For incident reports, Lea wants a timestamped timeline before the impact discussion. This ordering applies only to the incident-report task.

records.title: Lea at the Quill book club
records.body: The Book Club's Lea prefers chapter summaries ordered by character. This is a different person in a different project.

records.title: Reader study observation
records.body: Synthetic readers found the changed behavior in the first sentence of the new entries. The exercise did not measure whether migration checklists prevent mistakes.

records.title: Emoji heading suggestion
records.body: A writer suggested adding an emoji to every release-note heading. Lea has not expressed a preference about that suggestion.

records.title: Translation handoff note
records.body: Release-note examples should keep sample filenames unchanged during translation. Explanatory prose may be translated, but changing the filename breaks cross-language support references.

records.title: Queue age paging threshold
records.body: Beacon pages the primary responder when the oldest queued job exceeds eight minutes for three consecutive samples. A single slow sample only adds a dashboard marker.

records.title: Queue age sample interval
records.body: The queue-age watcher samples every thirty seconds. Consecutive samples reset when the oldest job drops back to eight minutes or less.

records.title: Pager state machine
records.body: advanceAgeAlarm in monitor/age_alarm.go tracks consecutive over-limit samples. Its page transition emits QUEUE_AGE_PAGE with the responder rotation key.

records.title: Quiet-hours exception
records.body: Queue-age pages are exempt from Beacon's quiet hours because delayed background dispatch can block customer work. Informational dashboard markers remain silent overnight.

records.title: Earlier single-sample paging
records.body: Beacon previously paged on one sample above five minutes. Short dispatch pauses produced noisy pages.

records.title: Noise reduction decision
records.body: The three-sample, eight-minute condition replaced single-sample paging. The thirty-second sampling cadence stayed unchanged.

records.title: Beacon battery warning
records.body: The hardware-health task warns when a sensor battery falls below fifteen percent. It routes to a maintenance inbox, not the primary responder.

records.title: Interrupted threshold run
records.body: The synthetic sample series nine, nine, seven, nine minutes did not page. The seven-minute sample reset the consecutive counter.

records.title: Unapproved percentile alarm
records.body: Omar proposed paging on the ninety-fifth percentile job age, but the proposal has not replaced oldest-job sampling.

records.title: Unretained escalation phone list
records.body: A draft phone list claims to name the backup responder. Its source attachment is missing, so the list cannot establish the current backup number.

records.title: Stoneware firing target
records.body: The Kiln stoneware program targets cone six. Earthenware bisque is a different program and must not inherit this target.

records.title: Controlled cooling hold
records.body: After stoneware reaches peak temperature, Kiln holds the cooling ramp at 1050 degrees Celsius for twenty minutes to stabilize the glaze surface.

records.title: Program ramp assembler
records.body: buildStonewareRamp in furnace/programs/stoneware.py inserts the twenty-minute cooling hold. Its HOLD_TEMP_C value is 1050.

records.title: Shelf clearance note
records.body: Stoneware shelves need at least twenty millimeters of clearance above the tallest piece. The clearance instruction concerns placement, not target cone.

records.title: Old cooling hold
records.body: The early stoneware recipe paused at 1100 degrees Celsius for ten minutes.

records.title: Glaze pinhole adjustment
records.body: The accepted glaze adjustment moved the hold to 1050 degrees Celsius and doubled it to twenty minutes. The target cone remained six.

records.title: Bisque program target
records.body: The bisque task uses cone zero-four with the vent open during the early ramp. These instructions do not define the stoneware program.

records.title: Pia's batch log preference
records.body: Pia wants batch logs to record the actual witness-cone bend in words alongside the programmed target. A set point alone is not an observation of the firing.

records.title: Glaze tile inspection
records.body: Synthetic test tiles showed fewer pinholes after the adjusted hold. The note supports the specific comparison but does not establish results for every glaze.

records.title: Fan acceleration idea
records.body: A helper suggested forcing cooling with a portable fan. No approved firing instruction or inspection supports that method.

records.title: Color grid keyboard motion
records.body: Mosaic's color grid moves one swatch with each arrow key. Home selects the first swatch in the current row; End selects the last.

records.title: Swatch focus policy
records.body: The color picker uses a single tab stop and roving focus inside the grid. Arrow movement previews a swatch, while Enter commits the color.

records.title: Swatch key handler
records.body: handleSwatchKey in ui/color/swatch_keys.ts distinguishes preview movement from commit. COLOR_COMMIT is dispatched only for Enter or a pointer activation.

records.title: Accessible swatch names
records.body: Each swatch's accessible name combines its human color name and hex value. Selection state is exposed separately, so the name does not grow every time the color changes.

records.title: Former tab-per-swatch interaction
records.body: The original color picker put every swatch into the page tab order.

records.title: Shorter keyboard traversal
records.body: A single tab stop replaced tab-per-swatch navigation so users could pass the picker without traversing the entire palette.

records.title: Mosaic tile inventory colors
records.body: The warehouse task uses color names as inventory variants. Keyboard arrow keys there move between stock-count cells, not swatches.

records.title: Ana's picker feedback preference
records.body: Ana wants the preview color shown beside the current committed color. The preview should be labeled so users can cancel without confusing it with a saved change.

records.title: Keyboard commit observation
records.body: A synthetic Right-Right-Escape sequence moved the preview twice and left the committed color unchanged. Replacing Escape with Enter committed the preview.

records.title: Completed case retention
records.body: Cedar retains completed case documents for eighteen months after case closure. Reopening a case suspends that countdown until the next closure.

records.title: Document hold precedence
records.body: An active preservation hold prevents expiry of every document attached to the case, even if its ordinary retention date has passed.

records.title: Retention deadline evaluator
records.body: effectiveExpiry in archive/retention_dates.py returns no deadline while a case is open or held. Otherwise it adds eighteen months to closed_at.

records.title: Previous closure retention
records.body: The original Cedar rule expired completed cases twelve months after closure.

records.title: Retention extension decision
records.body: Cedar extended completed-case retention to eighteen months to support the annual review cycle. Preservation holds continued to take precedence.

records.title: Preview derivative cache
records.body: The preview task discards rendered document thumbnails after seven idle days. Original case documents follow their own retention schedule.

records.title: Reopened case observation
records.body: A synthetic case closed in January and reopened in April had no effective expiry while open. Closing it again in June restarted the eighteen-month interval.

records.title: Bram's hold display preference
records.body: Bram wants a held case to show the hold reason before any estimated expiry date. An empty deadline should read Held, not Unknown.

records.title: Unretained hold notice
records.body: A copied email claims the Birch case is held, but the underlying notice was not retained. The copied claim cannot establish an active preservation hold.

records.title: Partition-local sequence contract
records.body: Relay orders events within one account partition by its sequence number. The public contract makes no total-order promise across different accounts.

records.title: Sequence merge implementation
records.body: mergePartitionEvents in streams/account_merge.rs sorts only events sharing an account key. CROSS_ACCOUNT_ORDER_UNDEFINED marks a request for a global sequence.

records.title: Clock-order proposal
records.body: Dina's design proposal orders unrelated accounts by producer wall-clock time. It is disputed because clocks can drift between producers.

records.title: Broker-order proposal
records.body: Milo's competing proposal orders unrelated accounts by broker arrival time. It is disputed because reconnects can rearrange the arrival of earlier producer events.

records.title: Ordering disagreement review
records.body: The shared review retained partition-local ordering. Neither wall-clock order nor broker-arrival order was accepted as a global causal order; a later decision would require a new contract.

records.title: Reconnect ordering observation
records.body: A synthetic reconnect delivered an older event from account B after a newer event from account A. Both accounts preserved their own sequence numbers.

records.title: Withdrawn global-order description
records.body: An early overview said all Relay events appeared in one causal order. Review withdrew this wording because the implementation only tracked account-local sequences.

records.title: Audit presentation ordering
records.body: The audit-view task sorts displayed rows by receipt time for readability. That visual sorting does not change event causality.

records.title: Dina's ordering terminology
records.body: Dina prefers the phrase account-local order in user documentation. She asks writers to avoid guaranteed global chronology.

records.title: Missing broker benchmark
records.body: A note claims broker-arrival ordering reduced reconciliation errors, but its experiment log is missing and no error counts survive.

records.title: Canary rollback gate
records.body: Ember rolls back a canary when its error rate exceeds the stable cohort by two percentage points for five minutes. An absolute error count alone does not trigger this gate.

records.title: Canary comparator
records.body: compareCanaryWindow in deploy/canary_window.go subtracts stable_error_fraction from canary_error_fraction. CANARY_DELTA_HIGH is emitted when the sustained delta crosses the configured limit.

records.title: Rollback artifact identity
records.body: A rollback deploys the exact artifact digest recorded for the previous accepted release. Rebuilding the previous branch is not considered an equivalent rollback.

records.title: Canary rollout rehearsal
records.body:
The Ember rehearsal began with two cohorts serving the same synthetic request mix. The dashboard showed request volume, response classes, and the image digest assigned to each cohort. Operators first confirmed that the stable cohort had enough traffic to provide a meaningful comparison. A sparse stable cohort was marked insufficient rather than silently treated as error-free.

The next stage exercised a short burst of server errors. The burst exceeded the delta limit but stopped before the five-minute observation window completed, so no automated rollback happened. A second burst persisted through the full window and generated a canary alarm. Both cohorts continued recording requests during the investigation, and the journal preserved the accepted stable digest alongside the candidate digest.

A separate exercise concerned the user interface. The operator could pause a rollout, inspect cohort details, and acknowledge an alarm. Those controls were visible on the same page, but they had different meanings. Acknowledging an alarm removed the unread indicator; it did not accept the release, clear the metric window, or change the rollback artifact.

At the final rehearsal step, the rollback target was selected from the last accepted artifact digest in the release ledger. The decisive condition was that an operator pause stops further traffic expansion but does not disable the canary rollback gate. A paused canary can still roll back when the sustained error delta qualifies.

records.title: Former rollback target selection
records.body: The early Ember script rebuilt the previous release branch to obtain a rollback image.

records.title: Artifact pinning decision
records.body: The release ledger now retains the accepted image digest so rollback can restore tested bytes. This replaces the branch-rebuild script.

records.title: Staging smoke alarm
records.body: The staging-smoke task fails immediately on any synthetic login error. It has no stable-cohort comparison and does not operate production canaries.

records.title: Tess's rollout panel preference
records.body: Tess wants the stable and canary image digests visible together before a rollout is expanded. A friendly release name may appear beside each digest.

records.title: Automatic pause exemption idea
records.body: A proposal would exempt paused canaries from rollback checks to make debugging easier. It has not been accepted.

records.title: Search cache identity
records.body: Fern keys cached search results by normalized query, locale, and catalog generation. A query string alone is insufficient because translated catalogs can differ.

records.title: Search cache lifetime
records.body: Search results expire after ninety seconds. Publishing a new catalog generation invalidates the old generation immediately rather than waiting for that timer.

records.title: Search cache key encoder
records.body: encodeSearchKey in search/cache_key.ts serializes locale before catalog generation and normalized query. CACHE_KEY_V2 names this tuple format.

records.title: Empty-result caching decision
records.body: Fern caches an empty result set for only fifteen seconds. A no-results response therefore does not inherit the ninety-second positive-result lifetime.

records.title: Query-only cache keys
records.body: The pilot cached search results using only the normalized query. Switching locale could show the previous language's catalog.

records.title: Locale-aware cache revision
records.body: Locale and catalog generation were added to the cache key to isolate translations and catalog publications. The normalized-query field stayed in the key.

records.title: Image thumbnail cache
records.body: The image-cache task retains thumbnails for two hours and keys them by source-image digest. It does not share search-result keys.

records.title: Locale switch observation
records.body: A synthetic switch from English to French produced separate search-cache entries for the same normalized query under one catalog generation.

records.title: Cache persistence assumption
records.body: Yuki wondered whether restarting the process would preserve search-cache entries. No persistence contract or restart measurement supports that assumption.

records.title: Yuki's cache diagnostics preference
records.body: Yuki wants locale and catalog generation shown when inspecting a search-cache hit. The raw user query should not be copied into diagnostics by default.

records.title: Calendar export timezone
records.body: Lumen exports timed calendar events using the event's stored IANA timezone. The computer's current local zone must not replace the event zone.

records.title: All-day export representation
records.body: All-day events export date values without a time or timezone suffix. Turning them into midnight instants can shift their apparent date for recipients.

records.title: Calendar date serializer
records.body: serializeCalendarDate in calendar/ical_dates.py selects a date-only branch for all_day entries. Timed entries carry TZID and a local wall time.

records.title: Former machine-zone export
records.body: The first exporter converted every timed event to the workstation's local timezone before writing the calendar file.

records.title: Event-zone preservation
records.body: The export revision preserved each event's stored timezone to prevent workstation settings from changing the file's meaning.

records.title: Repeated wall-time decision
records.body: When a timed event falls in a repeated daylight-saving hour, Lumen retains the event's stored offset choice. Export must not silently choose the first occurrence.

records.title: Agenda display zone
records.body: The agenda-view task can display all events in the viewer's chosen zone. That presentation setting does not rewrite the event's stored export zone.

records.title: Esme's event detail preference
records.body: Esme wants the event's zone name shown beside a timed event before export. All-day details should show the date without a fake midnight time.

records.title: Workstation-zone switch
records.body: A synthetic timed event stored in Europe/Paris exported with the same TZID after the workstation display was changed to America/Denver.

records.title: Unretained attendee timezone note
records.body: A copied note says the guest prefers Asia/Tokyo, but its source was not retained and the guest's preference is not confirmed.

records.title: Additive migration phases
records.body: Rivet adds the nullable column first, backfills existing rows second, and only then enables the non-null constraint. Readers must tolerate missing values during backfill.

records.title: Backfill checkpoint writer
records.body: saveBackfillCursor in migrations/cursor_store.sql persists the last completed primary key. MIGRATION_CURSOR advances only after the row batch commits.

records.title: Backfill transaction bound
records.body: Each Rivet backfill transaction covers at most two hundred rows. The next batch resumes after the last committed primary key, not after the last row read.

records.title: Backfill replay decision
records.body: A retried batch may revisit rows, so the derived column assignment must be idempotent. The checkpoint is not advanced for an aborted transaction.

records.title: Former read-position checkpoint
records.body: The pilot wrote its cursor after reading a batch, before committing the updated rows. A crash could skip the uncommitted batch.

records.title: Commit-bound cursor revision
records.body: The cursor now advances in the same transaction as the batch's updated rows. This replaced the read-position checkpoint and closed the skipped-batch gap.

records.title: Data-export cursor
records.body: The data-export task records the last emitted row number in an output file. It does not share schema-upgrade transaction checkpoints.

records.title: Aborted batch rehearsal
records.body: A synthetic failure before commit left both the derived values and migration cursor unchanged. Retrying then processed the same primary-key range.

records.title: Jon's progress display preference
records.body: Jon wants migration progress to count committed rows. Rows merely read into a pending batch should not increase the completed count.

records.title: Larger batch proposal
records.body: Jon proposed increasing batches to two thousand rows, but no accepted change or lock-duration measurement supports the increase.

records.title: Title search weighting
records.body: Summit gives a matching document title twice the lexical weight of the same term in a paragraph. Exact title matches do not bypass project visibility filters.

records.title: Expedition note aliases
records.body: Within Summit, acclimatization log and altitude diary name the same class of expedition note. The alias table expands either phrase at query time.

records.title: Alias expansion module
records.body: expandNoteAliases in search/query_aliases.py adds the alternate phrase while preserving the original query. NOTE_ALIAS_VERSION identifies the active table.

records.title: Search revision choice
records.body: The shared search contract says ordinary Summit searches return the newest published document revision. A historical revision is eligible only when the query explicitly requests it.

records.title: Former body-only lexical search
records.body: Summit's pilot indexed paragraph bodies and ignored document titles.

records.title: Title-index decision
records.body: Titles joined the lexical index because expedition leaders often remembered a note's heading. Their weight was set to twice the body-term weight.

records.title: Summit route planner names
records.body: The route-planning task uses altitude diary as the name of an elevation chart. It is a plotted route artifact, not an expedition note alias.

records.title: Sol's search result preference
records.body: Sol wants each search result to show its project name and published revision beside the title. A relevance score alone is not useful navigation context.

records.title: Alias search observation
records.body: In a synthetic expedition collection, altitude diary found a published acclimatization log despite the body using only the latter phrase.

records.title: Unretained summit report
records.body: A catalog note claims a summit report measured oxygen recovery, but the report body and its cited attachment were never retained.

records.title: Dawn watering quota
records.body: Orchard allocates nine liters to each young pear tree at dawn. Mature apple rows use a separate schedule; the pear quota should not be copied to them.

records.title: Pear valve lookup
records.body: resolvePearValve in control/rows/pear_valves.py maps a row label to its physical valve channel. Missing labels produce PEAR_ROW_UNKNOWN; the function does not infer a neighboring channel.

records.title: Rainfall pause decision
records.body: The watering controller skips the dawn pear cycle when the previous six hours recorded at least four millimeters of rain. It resumes at the next eligible dawn, without making up the skipped volume.

records.title: Early pear quota
records.body: The pilot applied twelve liters per young pear tree. The trial notes predate the soil retention survey.

records.title: Soil retention adjustment
records.body: The soil survey found puddling around young pears. The accepted adjustment reduced their dawn allocation from twelve to nine liters; other fruit rows were unaffected.

records.title: Mara wants amounts before confirmation
records.body: Mara asks the watering control to display liters per tree before opening a valve. She prefers a written amount to a slider percentage because volunteers rotate between rows.

records.title: Pear crate label color
records.body: The Orchard harvest task uses blue labels for pear crates and orange labels for apples. Label colors carry no watering instruction.

records.title: Orchard community garden
records.body: At the unrelated Hill Garden project, a bed nicknamed Orchard receives three liters each evening. Mara's orchard controls cannot address this garden's tap.

records.title: Rain gauge pause observation
records.body: A simulated rainfall total of 4.2 millimeters suppressed the dawn pear cycle. At 3.8 millimeters the scheduled cycle remained enabled.

records.title: Unretained frost forecast
records.body: A copied note predicts frost on the east pear row at dawn, but its forecast attachment was not retained. The note does not establish a verified frost threshold.

records.title: Foot passenger boarding cutoff
records.body: Tide closes foot-passenger boarding twelve minutes before the scheduled ferry departure. The arrival of a connecting bus does not extend that cutoff.

records.title: Vehicle check-in interval
records.body: Vehicles must reach the ferry staging lane forty minutes before departure. This vehicle check-in requirement is separate from foot-passenger boarding.

records.title: Boarding time evaluator
records.body: boardingDeadline in ferry/boarding_clock.py subtracts twelve minutes from scheduled_departure for a foot ticket. BOARDING_CLOSED means that deadline has passed.

records.title: Weather rescheduling decision
records.body: When weather changes the scheduled ferry departure, Tide recalculates boarding deadlines from the revised departure. A simple late-running notification does not change the schedule.

records.title: Pilot foot-boarding cutoff
records.body: The pilot closed foot-passenger boarding five minutes before departure.

records.title: Boarding safety buffer
records.body: Tide increased the foot-passenger buffer to twelve minutes so crew could complete the final passenger count before ramp closure.

records.title: Connecting bus boarding
records.body: The shuttle-booking task lets bus passengers board until the driver closes the door. Its timing does not govern the ferry ramp.

records.title: Oren's departure notice preference
records.body: Oren wants a changed departure notice to show both the revised sailing time and the recalculated boarding cutoff. A notice that only says Delayed is insufficient.

records.title: Revised sailing rehearsal
records.body: For a synthetic sailing moved from 09:00 to 09:30, Tide recalculated the foot boarding cutoff from 08:48 to 09:18.

records.title: Unretained bus guarantee
records.body: A copied travel note claims the ferry will wait for a particular bus, but the cited carrier agreement is missing.

records.title: Fastener count unit
records.body: Cobalt stores brass washer stock as individual pieces. Supplier cartons may contain different quantities, so carton count is recorded separately from available pieces.

records.title: Reservation arithmetic
records.body: Available washer stock equals on-hand pieces minus active reservations. Damaged pieces are removed from on-hand stock before this calculation.

records.title: Stock balance calculator
records.body: availablePieces in stock/balance.rs subtracts reserved_pieces from on_hand_pieces. STOCK_NEGATIVE flags a contradictory count rather than silently clipping it to zero.

records.title: Lot traceability decision
records.body: A washer reservation names a specific supplier lot. Substitution from another lot requires the pick list to be reissued so the shipment trace remains accurate.

records.title: Former carton-based inventory
records.body: The first Cobalt sheet treated one carton as one stock unit regardless of its contained quantity.

records.title: Piece-count migration
records.body: Cobalt moved from carton units to individual-piece counts after suppliers changed package sizes. Carton metadata remained available for receiving staff.

records.title: Cobalt paint stock
records.body: The paint-room task calls its blue pigment Cobalt and measures it in grams. Washer counts must not use this pigment's unit.

records.title: Vera's pick-list preference
records.body: Vera wants lot code and reserved piece count on the same pick-list line. A carton symbol alone does not tell a picker how many washers to take.

records.title: Damaged stock example
records.body: A synthetic lot started with fifty pieces, lost four damaged pieces, and reserved ten. Its available balance was thirty-six pieces.

records.title: Mixed-lot picking suggestion
records.body: A helper proposed combining visually identical washer lots on one reservation. The traceability owner has not accepted that suggestion.

records.title: Narration clip format
records.body: Juniper's narration clips use mono PCM at 24 kHz with sixteen-bit samples. The package manifest records duration in sample frames, not compressed-file bytes.

records.title: Leading silence allowance
records.body: A narration clip may contain at most 120 milliseconds of leading silence. The editor shows a warning beyond that allowance but preserves the original audio until the user trims it.

records.title: Clip header validator
records.body: validateNarrationHeader in audio/clip_header.py checks channel count, sample rate, and sample width. NARRATION_FORMAT_MISMATCH identifies a rejected header.

records.title: Narration packaging investigation
records.body:
The Juniper investigation began with a collection of short spoken prompts recorded for an invented museum exhibit. The editor displayed a waveform and let a narrator mark a preferred listening range without altering the source clip. Each source file had a checksum in the package manifest, and the listening range was represented by frame offsets.

Early checks concentrated on channel count and sample rate. Stereo clips were identified before package assembly, and the validation report grouped failures by their header fields. A different pass looked for long leading silence. That pass produced editorial warnings because an intentional pause can be meaningful to a narrator. The warning did not itself grant permission to rewrite the source audio.

One reviewer asked whether the visual selection changed the bytes that playback would use. Another asked whether the warning threshold was a hard import failure. The investigation kept those questions separate. The waveform's shaded selection was useful to an editor, but a shaded region alone was not a stored trim operation. The package continued to reference the original source checksum until an explicit edit was saved.

The final packing check supplied the decisive rule: clip end_frame is exclusive. A range starting at frame 100 and ending at frame 340 contains 240 frames. Package assembly must preserve this half-open boundary when creating the playback segment; treating the end frame as inclusive adds an unwanted sample.

records.title: Pilot narration rate
records.body: The narration pilot used 22.05 kHz mono PCM with sixteen-bit samples.

records.title: Narration rate revision
records.body: The narration rate changed to 24 kHz to match the exhibit playback device. Channel count and sample width stayed unchanged.

records.title: Music bed format
records.body: The music-bed task uses stereo audio at 48 kHz. Its format does not apply to short spoken narration clips.

records.title: Hugo's trim review preference
records.body: Hugo wants to hear the first half-second after a trim before saving it. He prefers an audible review to trusting the waveform alone.

records.title: Lossy archive proposal
records.body: A proposal would discard PCM sources after making small compressed previews. It is disputed because later edits need the original samples.

records.title: Imported coordinate order
records.body: Slate's point CSV format places longitude before latitude. This file convention is explicit even when a map label displays latitude first.

records.title: Coordinate range checks
records.body: Point import accepts longitude from minus 180 through 180 and latitude from minus 90 through 90, including endpoints. An out-of-range row is rejected rather than wrapped.

records.title: Point row parser
records.body: parsePointRow in geo/csv_points.rs reads longitude from column one and latitude from column two. POINT_AXIS_RANGE marks a coordinate outside the allowed interval.

records.title: Shared point reference-system contract
records.body: The shared Slate import contract fixes point CSV coordinates to WGS 84 longitude and latitude. A projected easting/northing file requires a separately declared importer and cannot reuse this CSV contract.

records.title: Former latitude-first pilot
records.body: The pilot point importer read latitude before longitude.

records.title: Axis convention revision
records.body: Slate adopted longitude-first files to match the geospatial interchange used by its partners. Existing pilot files require explicit conversion.

records.title: Map label coordinate order
records.body: The map-label task writes latitude before longitude in a human-readable tooltip. Tooltip presentation does not define the import column order.

records.title: Mina's import preview preference
records.body: Mina wants named Longitude and Latitude headings above the preview columns. She does not want bare X and Y labels for this geographic CSV format.

records.title: Boundary coordinate trial
records.body: The synthetic point 180, 90 passed range checks. The point 181, 45 was rejected without conversion to minus 179 longitude.

records.title: Unretained survey projection note
records.body: A survey note claims a local projected grid for the East Field file, but its reference-system definition is missing.

records.title: Missed-run behavior
records.body: Willow's daily digest job runs once after a short outage if today's scheduled run was missed. It does not replay every missed day after a week-long outage.

records.title: Digest overlap decision
records.body: Only one daily digest execution may be active for a workspace. If the previous run is still active at the next scheduled time, the new occurrence is marked skipped-overlap.

records.title: Occurrence claim function
records.body: claimDigestOccurrence in jobs/digest_claim.sql inserts a workspace-and-local-date key. DIGEST_ALREADY_CLAIMED means that occurrence has already been claimed.

records.title: Digest schedule zone
records.body: The daily digest schedule follows the workspace's stored timezone. Changing a viewer's display timezone does not move the scheduled occurrence.

records.title: Old outage replay behavior
records.body: The prototype replayed a digest for each missed calendar day after an outage.

records.title: Digest catch-up revision
records.body: Willow replaced multi-day replay with one catch-up for the current day to avoid sending a burst of obsolete summaries.

records.title: Nightly backup catch-up
records.body: The backup task queues a replacement backup after recovery even if the daily digest has already run. Backup occurrences have their own claim keys.

records.title: Rafi's skipped-run preference
records.body: Rafi wants skipped-overlap shown with the still-running occurrence link. A generic Failed label would imply the skipped job executed and broke.

records.title: Repeated claim observation
records.body: A synthetic second claim for the same workspace and local date returned DIGEST_ALREADY_CLAIMED. A claim for the following date used a different key.

records.title: Minute-level retry proposal
records.body: Rafi suggested trying overlap-skipped digests every minute until the earlier run ends. The suggestion is unapproved and no retry loop exists in the recorded design.

records.title: Precision tool loan period
records.body: Copper loans a precision torque wrench for three working days. Weekend days do not count; ordinary workshop spanners use a different category.

records.title: Calibration eligibility
records.body: A torque wrench with an expired calibration label cannot be checked out. Renewing a loan does not extend the instrument's calibration validity.

records.title: Tool eligibility routine
records.body: canLoanInstrument in loans/instrument_rules.py checks calibration_valid_until before creating a loan. CALIBRATION_EXPIRED blocks checkout even when the tool is physically present.

records.title: Torque wrench renewal rule
records.body: A borrower may renew a torque wrench once for two additional working days if nobody has reserved it. A pending reservation prevents renewal.

records.title: Former calendar-day torque loan
records.body: The pilot required a torque wrench back after three calendar days, including weekends.

records.title: Working-day loan decision
records.body: Copper changed precision tool loans to working days because the workshop is closed on weekends. The one-renewal limit stayed in place.

records.title: Ordinary spanner checkout
records.body: The general-tools task loans ordinary spanners until the end of the current workshop session. It does not require an instrument calibration label.

records.title: Ivo's checkout screen preference
records.body: Ivo wants the calibration expiry and due date shown separately. One combined Valid until label can hide which constraint expires first.

records.title: Reserved wrench renewal trial
records.body: A synthetic wrench with valid calibration and a next-day reservation was refused renewal. Without the reservation its first renewal was accepted.

records.title: Tabular text delimiter
records.body: Opal's plain table importer expects tab-separated fields. Commas inside a field are ordinary text, not separators.

records.title: Empty field representation
records.body: An empty tab-separated field becomes a null value in Opal. The literal text NULL remains a four-character string unless a column-specific mapping is declared.

records.title: Table field decoder
records.body: decodeTabField in import/tab_fields.py preserves literal text and handles the empty-field sentinel. FIELD_COUNT_MISMATCH rejects rows with a different number of fields than the header.

records.title: Input text encoding
records.body: Plain table files must be UTF-8. A leading UTF-8 byte-order mark is accepted and removed from the first header name; it is not part of the column's identity.

records.title: Pilot null-word conversion
records.body: The first importer converted every case-insensitive NULL word into a null value, even in free-text columns.

records.title: Literal text preservation
records.body: Opal stopped globally converting the word NULL because notes could use it as ordinary text. Only empty fields or an explicit column mapping now produce nulls.

records.title: Spreadsheet import formulas
records.body: The workbook-import task reads displayed cell values from a spreadsheet. It does not execute formulas or apply the plain-table delimiter rule.

records.title: Nell's import error preference
records.body: Nell wants a malformed table row identified by its source line number and expected field count. The error display should not paste the entire row into shared logs.

records.title: Comma preservation trial
records.body: A synthetic field containing north, west remained one string in a tab-separated import. A blank neighboring field became null.

records.title: Unretained legacy character map
records.body: A note claims to map an old regional encoding to UTF-8, but the mapping table was not retained.

records.title: Stable flag allocation
records.body: Spruce assigns the new editor flag by hashing workspace ID with the rollout salt. Reloading a page does not randomly choose a new cohort.

records.title: Explicit flag override precedence
records.body: A workspace-specific disable override takes precedence over percentage rollout. Removing the override returns the workspace to its stable hashed cohort.

records.title: Editor cohort resolver
records.body: resolveEditorCohort in flags/editor_cohort.ts checks disable_override before the hash bucket. FLAG_DISABLED_OVERRIDE records why an otherwise eligible bucket is disabled.

records.title: Rollout salt preservation
records.body: Changing the rollout salt can reshuffle workspaces. Spruce keeps the salt stable when increasing the rollout percentage so existing assignments remain interpretable.

records.title: Session-random pilot
records.body: The editor pilot chose flag assignment randomly at each session start. One workspace could see different editors on successive sessions.

records.title: Workspace-cohort revision
records.body: Spruce replaced per-session random assignment with workspace hashing to keep collaborators in the same editor cohort.

records.title: Spruce email experiment
records.body: The email-experiment task assigns variants by recipient ID. That recipient-level experiment does not determine the workspace editor flag.

records.title: Alix's flag explanation preference
records.body: Alix wants the rollout panel to distinguish explicit disable from an out-of-percentage bucket. Both are off, but only the former is an operator override.

records.title: Disabled bucket observation
records.body: A synthetic workspace in an enabled hash bucket remained disabled while its override existed. Removing the override enabled its assigned cohort.

records.title: User-level editor flag idea
records.body: An unapproved proposal would let each user select an editor cohort independently. No accepted collaboration policy supports that change.

records.title: Water temperature aggregation window
records.body: Marina reports water temperature as the median of valid samples in a trailing ten-minute window. Invalid sensor readings are excluded before computing the median.

records.title: Minimum temperature sample count
records.body: A Marina temperature aggregate needs at least four valid samples in its window. With fewer samples, the report is unavailable rather than zero degrees.

records.title: Median sample reducer
records.body: reduceTemperatureWindow in sensors/temperature_window.py drops invalid readings and checks sample_count before selecting the median. TEMP_SAMPLES_INSUFFICIENT is the unavailable reason.

records.title: Buoy timestamp investigation
records.body:
The Marina buoy investigation used invented temperature packets with source timestamps and receiver timestamps. The monitoring page grouped packets by buoy and displayed a small graph of the most recent readings. A packet's arrival could be delayed by a radio retry, so arrival order was not always measurement order. The first review therefore separated transport delay from sensor temperature.

The aggregation exercise included valid readings, sensor-error markers, and a brief radio outage. Error markers appeared in the diagnostic log but did not become numeric temperatures. During the outage, the trailing window gradually lost older valid readings. Once fewer than four remained, the aggregate became unavailable. The display used a gap rather than extending the previous median indefinitely.

Another part of the exercise considered presentation precision. The dashboard rounded temperatures for display while retaining source values in the diagnostic record. That rounding rule did not determine which samples entered a window. The operator could inspect receiver delay and packet count, but neither number was a replacement for the measurement's own time.

The final finding resolved the window boundary: membership uses the sensor's measurement timestamp, not the packet's arrival time. A late packet measured eleven minutes before the report time is excluded even if it arrived one second ago. A valid packet measured two minutes ago can still contribute when it arrives late.

records.title: Former average reducer
records.body: The pilot used the arithmetic mean of temperature readings, allowing isolated extreme values to shift the reported aggregate.

records.title: Median reducer decision
records.body: Marina selected the median to reduce the influence of isolated extreme readings. The decision did not make invalid sensor readings eligible.

records.title: Wind gust aggregation
records.body: The wind-monitor task reports the maximum valid gust in a five-minute window. It does not share the temperature median reducer.

records.title: Bo's unavailable display preference
records.body: Bo wants an insufficient-samples temperature result shown as a gap with its reason. A displayed zero could be mistaken for a real freezing-water measurement.

records.title: Arrival-time window proposal
records.body: A proposed simplification would use packet arrival time for temperature windows. It remains disputed because radio delays could move old readings into a current report.

records.title: Missing conductivity calibration
records.body: A note claims a conductivity probe's calibration coefficient, but the calibration worksheet is missing and contains no retained numeric coefficient.

records.title: Manifest signature payload
records.body: Quartz signs the canonical manifest bytes after deterministic key ordering and UTF-8 encoding. A pretty-printed copy is for display and is not a substitute signature payload.

records.title: Release verification key selection
records.body: A release manifest identifies its signing key by key ID. Verification looks up that exact key ID in the release trust set rather than selecting the newest key automatically.

records.title: Canonical manifest serializer
records.body: canonicalManifestBytes in manifests/canonical.py emits sorted keys without insignificant whitespace. MANIFEST_DIGEST_MISMATCH means the fetched payload differs from its recorded digest.

records.title: Revoked release key policy
records.body: A revoked signing key cannot verify a newly accepted Quartz release. Historical inspection may show that a prior release was signed by the key, but it does not restore trust in the revoked key.

records.title: Former display-JSON signature input
records.body: The early prototype signed the same indented JSON shown in the release panel.

records.title: Canonical payload decision
records.body: Quartz separated canonical signature bytes from display formatting so whitespace changes in the panel cannot redefine the signed payload.

records.title: Preview manifest generator
records.body: The preview-build task emits unsigned manifests for local inspection. An unsigned preview is not eligible for release acceptance.

records.title: Faye's verification display preference
records.body: Faye wants the manifest digest and signing key ID visible together. A green verification icon without those identities is insufficient evidence for her review.

records.title: Whitespace rendering trial
records.body: A synthetic manifest displayed with different indentation retained the same canonical bytes and digest. Changing a dependency value produced different canonical bytes.

records.title: Unretained historical signature
records.body: A catalog entry claims an old release carried key Q7's signature, but the signature file was not retained.

records.title: Notebook section order
records.body: Birch exports notebook sections in their explicit outline order. Sorting by section title would change the author's intended reading sequence.

records.title: Internal notebook link targets
records.body: An internal notebook link targets a stable section anchor. Renaming a section changes its visible heading but preserves the anchor.

records.title: Outline export iterator
records.body: iterExportSections in notebooks/outline_export.py follows stored sibling order and omits deleted sections. SECTION_ANCHOR_MISSING identifies an unresolved internal target.

records.title: Notebook appendix export review
records.body:
The Birch export review used an invented laboratory notebook with a methods section, an observation log, and several appendices. Editors moved sections within the outline and renamed headings while keeping the notes themselves unchanged. A preview showed the reading order and let reviewers inspect internal links before saving a document.

The first checks focused on heading numbers. Moving an appendix changed its displayed number, but links continued to use stable section anchors. A renamed heading therefore did not require rewriting every internal reference. Deleted sections were excluded from export, and unresolved links were reported with their missing target anchor rather than silently redirected to a similarly named heading.

Later checks considered attachment presentation. Small illustrations appeared inline, while large source tables were listed as appendix attachments. The review recorded source checksums and display captions separately. A caption change was not treated as a change to the attachment's retained bytes. The reviewers also verified that an exported preview had the same outline order as the notebook.

The final appendix test established the decisive exclusion rule: a section marked private-draft remains absent from a shared export even if a public section links to it. That link becomes an unresolved-reference notice in the shared document; the link does not grant permission to include the private draft's body.

records.title: Alphabetical export pilot
records.body: The first notebook exporter sorted sections alphabetically by heading before writing them.

records.title: Outline-preserving export
records.body: Birch adopted stored outline order after alphabetic export separated explanations from their following examples.

records.title: Notebook title index
records.body: The notebook-index task sorts notebook titles alphabetically for navigation. That index ordering does not define section order within an export.

records.title: Uma's unresolved-link preference
records.body: Uma wants an unresolved internal link to show its target heading when known and a clear missing-reference label. A clickable link to the document's first page would hide the problem.

records.title: Draft-link inclusion proposal
records.body: A proposal would include a private draft whenever a public section links to it. It is disputed because references do not confer sharing permission.

records.title: Task handoff ownership
records.body: In Kestrel, a queued handoff remains owned by the sender until the recipient accepts it. Sending a handoff request alone does not transfer responsibility.

records.title: Accepted handoff record
records.body: An accepted handoff records sender, recipient, and acceptance time together. The recipient becomes the active owner at that recorded time.

records.title: Handoff acceptance transaction
records.body: acceptHandoff in workflow/handoff_store.sql changes active_owner and appends the acceptance record in one transaction. HANDOFF_STALE rejects an already replaced request.

records.title: Pending handoff withdrawal
records.body: The sender may withdraw an unaccepted handoff. Withdrawing a pending request leaves active ownership unchanged.

records.title: Send-time transfer pilot
records.body: Kestrel's pilot changed task owner when a handoff request was sent, before the recipient responded.

records.title: Acceptance-bound ownership decision
records.body: The shared Kestrel review made recipient acceptance the transfer boundary after the send-time pilot left unattended tasks. The sender retains responsibility until acceptance.

records.title: Notification handoff label
records.body: The notification task uses Handed off as the label for a message passed to a delivery worker. That label says nothing about human task ownership.

records.title: Gus's pending handoff preference
records.body: Gus wants both current owner and intended recipient visible while a handoff is pending. Showing only the recipient would imply acceptance already occurred.

records.title: Withdrawn request trial
records.body: A synthetic unaccepted handoff was withdrawn, and the sender remained active owner. A later attempt to accept that replaced request returned HANDOFF_STALE.

records.title: Unretained recipient acceptance note
records.body: A copied note claims that Dara accepted the Beacon task, but its acceptance record was not retained. The copy cannot establish a completed handoff.

records.title: Sensor white reference
records.body: Violet calibrates its color sensor against the supplied matte white reference tile. A glossy sheet of printer paper is not the designated reference.

records.title: Color sensor warm-up
records.body: The Violet sensor warms for ninety seconds before a calibration capture. Starting calibration earlier returns a warm-up state rather than a valid reading.

records.title: White capture controller
records.body: captureWhiteReference in sensor/white_capture.py checks warmup_elapsed and reference_present. WHITE_REFERENCE_PENDING means a prerequisite is not yet satisfied.

records.title: Open-shroud proposal
records.body: Ren proposed calibrating with the shroud open to simplify tile placement. The proposal is disputed because room lighting can contaminate the reading.

records.title: Closed-shroud proposal
records.body: Miko proposed calibrating with the shroud closed around the tile. This competing proposal is disputed pending a repeatability study of the placement mechanism.

records.title: Current shroud procedure
records.body: The current supported Violet procedure closes the shroud before white-reference capture. The open-shroud proposal has not replaced this procedure.

records.title: Short warm-up pilot
records.body: The sensor pilot allowed reference capture after thirty seconds of warm-up.

records.title: Warm-up stabilization revision
records.body: Violet extended warm-up from thirty to ninety seconds after early readings drifted. The matte reference tile stayed unchanged.

records.title: Ren's calibration screen preference
records.body: Ren wants remaining warm-up time shown as seconds, followed by a separate Ready to capture state. A frozen spinner gives no indication of progress.

records.title: Missing placement repeatability report
records.body: A note claims the closed shroud achieved a numerical repeatability target, but its measurement table is missing and no variance estimate is retained.

records.title: Parcel route priority
records.body: Delta chooses an explicitly assigned depot before considering postcode routing. A postcode match does not override a valid explicit depot assignment.

records.title: Postcode fallback route
records.body: Without an explicit depot, Delta selects the longest matching postcode prefix. A two-character regional prefix loses to a matching four-character district prefix.

records.title: Depot route resolver
records.body: resolveParcelDepot in parcels/depot_route.py checks explicit_depot and then longestPrefixMatch. DEPOT_ROUTE_UNKNOWN means neither route source produced an eligible depot.

records.title: Depot closure rehearsal
records.body:
The Delta routing rehearsal began with invented parcels assigned to several depots. Some parcels carried an explicit depot from an operator; others relied on postcode prefixes. The route preview showed the selected depot and the source of that choice. A short regional prefix covered a broad area, while longer district prefixes provided more specific fallback destinations.

The first test group changed parcel postcodes without touching explicit assignments. Those parcels retained their explicit depots, which confirmed precedence. A second group removed explicit assignments and then exercised postcode matching. Where both regional and district prefixes matched, the district mapping won because its prefix was longer. Rows with no usable mapping were marked unresolved for operator attention.

The operator panel also showed depot labels, opening notes, and the latest routing-table version. Those presentation details helped explain a route, but a depot's friendly label did not determine whether it could accept a parcel. A renamed depot kept its stable internal key. The rehearsal retained the before-and-after route choices so reviewers could distinguish a renamed destination from a changed destination.

The final closure exercise established the decisive rule: an explicit assignment to a closed depot is rejected and sent for operator review. Delta must not silently fall back to a postcode depot in that case. Fallback is permitted only when the explicit assignment is absent, not when an explicit instruction has become unusable.

records.title: Former first-prefix fallback
records.body: The pilot selected the first matching postcode prefix in file order, even when a later prefix was more specific.

records.title: Specific-prefix routing decision
records.body: Delta replaced file-order matching with longest-prefix matching so a district route could consistently override its broader regional fallback.

records.title: Return parcel depot
records.body: The returns-routing task directs parcels to the original dispatch depot when it remains eligible. It uses a separate rule from outbound postcode routing.

records.title: Zia's route review preference
records.body: Zia wants every route preview to name whether it came from an explicit assignment or a postcode prefix. Showing only the depot conceals why it was selected.

records.title: Closed-depot auto-fallback proposal
records.body: A suggestion would reroute closed-depot assignments automatically by postcode. It has not been accepted because it can override an operator's explicit instruction.
